retrieved.text: What counts as a billing error. A charge the cardholder didn't authorize; a charge that isn't identified properly; goods or services not accepted or not delivered as agreed; a payment or credit not posted properly; a computational error by the issuer; a request for clarification or documentation about a charge; failure to send a statement to the last known address.

Fraud routing. Any charge the cardholder says they didn't make or authorize goes to the fraud team on the same call. Block the card, reissue, open a fraud claim. Agents do not open these as billing disputes only.

Quality disputes (claims and defenses). A complaint about the quality of goods the cardholder accepted isn't a billing error. It may qualify as a claim against the issuer if the cardholder tried in good faith to resolve it with the merchant, the purchase was over $50, and it happened in the cardholder's state or within 100 miles of their address. The $50 and location limits don't apply when the merchant and issuer are related.

note: Cardholder Sabrina Kowalczyk reports a $310.00 charge from Lumen & Loft Decor on 2026-09-07 for a wall mirror that did not fit. The cardholder says they mailed it back in mid-September with no tracking number. The cardholder sent a general contact-form message to the merchant and has had no direct reply. No one confirmed receipt of the return or a refund, though the cardholder isn't sure whether anyone promised one. No dispute was opened. Unknown: statement date, whether the return arrived, refund status, and any written notice to the issuer. Escalated to supervisor (LOW_CONFIDENCE) to decide between the billing-error path (REG-01) and the quality-claim path (REG-13), which depends on the good-faith merchant attempt and the $50 and location limits.
